messages:
emma: Quick alert — saw a small but consistent invoice preview overcount for a group of tenants (~0.6%) between 08:10-08:40 UTC. ledger raw shows expected tokens, preview shows + duplicates. looks related to multi-replica routing fanout we rolled last week
raj: interesting. I remember the fanout change: for low-latency we send to primary + warm replica in parallel and pick first response. did we also emit metering events for both replicas?
sophia: yes, edge emits attempt events per replica with attempt_index (0/1). ingest was supposed to dedupe by client_request_id but our proxy rewrites request_id per replica to help tracing, so dedupe missed them
noah: can confirm we get two metering events with different request_id but same client_req_id in headers. aggregator keys on request_id currently
emma: partial mitigation idea: propagate a stable "client_req_id" header into the metering events and have the aggregator prefer dedupe by client_req_id when present. cheaper than altering request_id rewrite behavior
raj: downside: some older clients don't set client_req_id. we could generate a stable edge-side client_req_id derived from incoming connection+seq for those cases. but must be careful for proxies that pool connections
sophia: alternative: emit sequence_number from proxy per incoming client request and carry it through replicas. sequence_number + tenant_id should be unique and deterministic for the request across replicas
noah: sample pseudo for edge:
```
# on accept
if headers.get('x-client-req'):
  client_req = headers['x-client-req']
else:
  client_req = sha256(conn_id + ':' + str(conn_seq))
for attempt_idx, backend in replicas:
  event = make_event(...)
  event['client_req_id'] = client_req
  event['replica_idx'] = attempt_idx
  emit(event)
```
emma: nice. aggregator changes: 1) check client_req_id dedupe within dedupe_window 2) prefer client_req_id over request_id if present 3) when deduping emit tombstone events (counted_but_deduped=true) so console can show pre/post numbers
raj: sampling implications: our preview sampler samples upstream of aggregator. if we dedupe later, preview might still show inflated numbers. so we either move sampling after dedupe or propagate a sampled flag and re-sample post-aggregator
sophia: moving sampling after dedupe is conceptually simpler but might increase latency for preview generation. other trade is to have a tiny lightweight dedupe stage just for preview that uses client_req_id and runs fast
noah: ops checklist suggestion:
- edge: emit client_req_id (canary)
- ingress: minor PR to ensure header passthrough to metering event
- aggregator: dedupe by client_req_id and tombstone emit
- preview: move sampling post-dedupe or add preview-dedupe shim
- console: add pre/post token card + explanation tooltip
- backfill: detection job to scan last 48h for duplicated client_req patterns and emit correction events
emma: canary plan: 1h on 30 tenants starting 01:00 UTC. I'll own canary selection. alert if dedupe_rate > 0.2% or invoice delta > 0.5%
raj: I'll own edge patch and quick perf test (hashing + header gen). keep overhead minimal (sha256 ok but maybe siphash faster)
sophia: I'll do aggregator PR and preview shim tests. include unit tests for race with simultaneous replica emits
noah: console work: small UI card showing "tokens_raw / tokens_final (post-dedupe)". also link to ticket MET-5219 in tooltip
ops-bot: MET-5219 created by emma: "metering: dedupe replica-fanout attempts using client_req_id to prevent invoice double-counts". priority P2. owners: emma/raj/sophia/noah. canary 01:00 UTC
emma: final note: add a short runbook entry to oncall: if routing fanout enabled, check client_req_dedupe_rate metric and preview vs ledger alignment. saves triage time
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: MET-5219 canary kickoff 01:00 UTC tomorrow
